user.title: Add a Mysa thermostat
user.description:
Mysa Local controls Mysa thermostats over your own network (HomeKit), with Mysa's cloud as an optional extra.

Tested so far on the Mysa Baseboard Lite (BB-V2-0-L). Other models are supported through Mysa's capability data but are untested.

menu_options.takeover: Move a thermostat from the HomeKit Device integration
menu_options.cloud_login: Sign in to Mysa and add thermostats from my account

wifi_help.title: Put the thermostat on Wi-Fi
wifi_help.description:
A new or reset Mysa shows a Bluetooth icon. Put it on your 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi with the browser-based setup page: [{url}]({url}). It works in Chrome or Edge on a computer with Bluetooth, with no Mysa app and no phone.

Once it's on Wi-Fi, Home Assistant discovers it. Submit to go back.

pick.title: Pick a thermostat
pick.description: Unpaired Mysa thermostats found on your network. If yours isn't listed, check it's on Wi-Fi ([setup page]({url})) and that it isn't paired to Apple Home or another controller.

pair.title: Pair {name}
pair.description:
Enter the 8-digit HomeKit setup code for {name} ({model}). It's printed on the back of the faceplate.

A thermostat can only be paired to one HomeKit controller. If it's in Apple Home, remove it there first. {error}

takeover_confirm.title: Move {name} to Mysa Local
takeover_confirm.description: Mysa Local adds its own HomeKit pairing to {name} through the existing one, so you don't need the setup code. Its entities keep their entity IDs, names and area, and the HomeKit Device entry is removed afterwards. {error}

cloud_offer.title: Mysa cloud (optional)
cloud_offer.description:
Signing in to your Mysa account adds what HomeKit doesn't expose: button lock, display brightness, setpoint limits, temperature offset, heater type, schedules and holds, firmware updates and the thermostat's own heating runtime. It also keeps control working if the local connection drops.

You can skip this and sign in later from the integration's options.

cloud_login.title: Sign in to Mysa
cloud_login.description: Your password is only used to sign in and isn't stored; Home Assistant keeps a sign-in token instead.

cloud_devices.title: Thermostats from your account
cloud_devices.description: These are controlled through Mysa's cloud only. To add a thermostat locally later, pair it from the integration page.

finish.title: Untested model
finish.description: The {model} hasn't been tested with Mysa Local yet. It should work through Mysa's capability data, but some features may be missing or wrong. After setup, please download the diagnostics and share them in an issue on GitHub, so it can be marked as tested.

reauth_confirm.title: Sign in to Mysa again
reauth_confirm.description: The stored Mysa sign-in stopped working. Local control keeps working in the meantime.

data_description.heater_watts: Total wattage of the heaters this thermostat switches. Set it to get an energy sensor for the Energy dashboard; 0 turns it off.
data_description.use_cloud_runtime: The thermostat measures its own on-time, which also covers periods when Home Assistant was down. Off: count it from the heating state that Home Assistant sees.

data_description.cloud_enabled: Off: no calls to Mysa's servers at all, and the cloud-only entities are removed. Your sign-in is kept, so turning it back on needs no password.
data_description.scan_interval: How often to read all thermostats from the cloud (one request per poll). Local HomeKit updates are instant regardless.

data_description.allow_firmware_install: Lets the Firmware entity install updates Mysa offers. Untested, and an install can't be undone.

sign_out.title: Sign out of Mysa
sign_out.description: Deletes the stored sign-in. Cloud-only entities are removed and thermostats added from the account stop working until you sign in again.

thermostat_unreachable.message: {name} can't be reached locally, and the Mysa cloud isn't available to fall back on.

local_required.message: {name} needs a working local (HomeKit) connection for this.

cloud_required.message: {name} needs the Mysa cloud for this. Sign in, or turn the cloud on, in the integration's options.

limits_invalid.message: The lowest setpoint must stay below the highest setpoint.

hold_in_past.message: The hold's end time is in the past.

firmware_timeout.message: {name} didn't report the new firmware within 6 minutes. Check it in a while.

local_unreachable.title: {name} isn't reachable on your network
local_unreachable.description:
Home Assistant hasn't reached {name} over HomeKit (last address {host}) for {minutes} minutes, and the Mysa cloud isn't available as a fallback.

Check that the thermostat has power and is on Wi-Fi, and give it a DHCP reservation on your router so its address doesn't change. This message clears itself once the thermostat is back.

local_unreachable_cloud.title: {name} is running on the Mysa cloud
local_unreachable_cloud.description:
Home Assistant hasn't reached {name} over HomeKit (last address {host}) for {minutes} minutes, so it's being controlled through Mysa's cloud for now.

Check that the thermostat is on the same network as Home Assistant, and give it a DHCP reservation on your router so its address doesn't change. This message clears itself once the local connection is back.

hold.name: Hold
hold.description: Holds a setpoint over the thermostat's Mysa schedule, permanently or until a time.

temperature.name: Temperature
temperature.description: Setpoint to hold. Defaults to the current setpoint.

hvac_mode.name: Mode
hvac_mode.description: Mode to hold. Defaults to the current mode.

until.name: Until
until.description: End of the hold. Leave empty for a permanent hold.

resume_schedule.name: Resume schedule
resume_schedule.description: Ends a hold, so the thermostat follows its Mysa schedule again.

set_schedule.name: Set schedule
set_schedule.description: Replaces the weekly schedule stored on Mysa's side. It keeps running even when Home Assistant or the internet is down.

events.name: Events
events.description: List of events, each with days (mon to sun), time (HH:MM), temperature and optionally hvac_mode.
